title: Scalar matrix inclusion of the multiplicative group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $r\geq1$. Use the group schemes and their morphisms over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme], the multiplicative group $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec} k[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-gm-ga], and the matrix scheme $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}=\operatorname{Spec} k[x_{ij},\det(x)^{-1}]$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Define the scalar matrix inclusion $s_{k,r}:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}$ to be the morphism induced by the $k$-algebra homomorphism $x_{ij}\mapsto t\delta_{ij}$, $\det(x)^{-1}\mapsto t^{-r}$. On every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ this is the scalar matrix map $A^\times\to\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$, $z\mapsto zI_r$, including nonreduced test algebras. The same coordinate substitution is defined also for $r=0$, when its target is the trivial matrix group.

source.place: Example 5.49, printed p.111 (Gm embedded diagonally in GL_n), and its coordinate scalar substitution.
